change: Added multilingual and extended database layer.
reason: Chinese, engineering, subscription, arXiv, and Semantic Scholar gaps identified.
impact_on_review: Current search cannot be described as exhaustive until expanded or limitations are reported.

change: Added AI-scientist-inspired reproducibility and governance layer.
reason: Need audit trail for automated search/screening/extraction.
impact_on_review: Adds reproducibility, false-negative mitigation, and manual adjudication requirements.

original_plan: Generic validation and risk-of-bias notes only.
change: Added Mohamed-style reproducibility benchmark; R0-R4 reproducibility maturity; voice-biomarker ML risk-of-bias domains; full-text extraction template; expanded seed set.
reason: Need stronger reproducibility controls before a submission-quality systematic review.
impact_on_review: Adds required extraction fields and may change full-text screening workload; does not change inclusion criteria.

change: Added seed supplement candidates for two missed seeds and added PMID/PMCID fields to full-text extraction template.
reason: False-negative audit showed two seed misses; full-text calibration requires stable biomedical identifiers.
impact_on_review: Improves auditability and full-text retrieval; does not change eligibility criteria.

original_plan: Formal search restricted to PubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, Crossref and arXiv.
change: Added Consensus as a supplementary (non-exhaustive) discovery tool and logged four newly discovered records.
reason: Needed an independent probe for false negatives before subscription and engineering databases become available.
impact_on_review: Confirms the IEEE/ACM/ACL coverage gap empirically; adds four candidates; does not change eligibility criteria. Consensus free tier caps results at 3 per query, so it must be reported as supplementary, never as a primary source of counts.

original_plan: Review described inconsistently as systematic mapping review, systematic review, and living review; reported against PRISMA 2020 only.
change: Fixed review type of record to systematic mapping review; adopted PRISMA-ScR as reporting guideline, PRISMA-S for search reporting, JBI guidance for conduct; dropped the 'living' claim; recorded that PROSPERO does not register mapping reviews and OSF is the registry.
reason: PRISMA 2020 governs systematic reviews of effectiveness and is the wrong guideline for a mapping synthesis; 'living' implies a re-search cadence that was never specified.
impact_on_review: Changes reporting checklist and manuscript methods framing. Does not change research questions, eligibility criteria, or any screening decision already made.

original_plan: Formal search used relevance sorting with a single 100-record page per source.
change: Switched all sources to deterministic date sorting with cursor/offset pagination up to 1000 records; truncation is now reported in the counts CSV; added scripts/test_search_api_contract.py as a live contract test; recorded SHA-256 manifest for the locally cached full-text HTML that is excluded from version control.
reason: Relevance ranking is not stable across time, so the Stage 1 search was not re-runnable, and single-page retrieval silently truncated large result sets; the audit trail also pointed at gitignored files.
impact_on_review: Stage 1 candidate CSVs and counts were produced by the previous non-deterministic code and must be regenerated before final synthesis; existing counts must be preserved in the search log when they are superseded. Does not change eligibility criteria.

original_plan: arXiv query was assembled automatically from the family label and an 80-character slice of the generic query string.
change: Gave each query family an explicit hand-written arXiv query in the arxiv field of QueryFamily, mirroring the existing pubmed field; added a regression test asserting the result set is plausibly scoped and topical.
reason: The assembled query had unbalanced quotes, so arXiv parsed it as a disjunction of bare words and matched its entire corpus (3,149,925 records). The defect was masked because arXiv previously failed with rate-limit and timeout errors on every attempt.
impact_on_review: Stage 1 reported arXiv as 'undercovered due to API failure'; the real position is that arXiv was never validly queried. Corrected per-family arXiv hit counts are 24, 7, 8, 30 and 254. No candidate record was ever admitted from the malformed query: the affected run was discarded before commit.

original_plan: Search fetchers had no retry logic and sent no User-Agent.
change: Added bounded retries with linear backoff to the search script and the contract test; set a descriptive User-Agent; made the OpenAlex polite-pool contact address opt-in through the OPENALEX_MAILTO environment variable.
reason: A single transient DNS failure aborted an entire query family and silently changed search coverage; nine of twenty-five source-family combinations failed this way on the first re-run attempt.
impact_on_review: Improves search completeness and reduces rate-limiting. A contact address is personal data sent to a third party, so it is opt-in and never hard-coded.

original_plan: Single disease_monitoring family combining bare terms (screening OR monitoring OR diagnosis) with a 14-item disease list.
change: Split into four disease subfamilies (neuro, psych, respiratory, cardiometabolic), each formed as (named voice/speech/acoustic construct) AND (disease terms). Eight families total.
reason: The old family matched 886,668 OpenAlex records against a 1,000-record ceiling, retrieving about 0.1 percent of its own result set; the bare monitoring terms, not the disease list, caused the explosion.
impact_on_review: Largest family now returns 4,000 records and every family retrieves completely under the raised 8,000 ceiling, so date-sorted truncation no longer over-samples recent work. Prior counts are preserved; the corpus must be rebuilt before synthesis counts are updated.

original_plan: Formal search limited to PubMed, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, arXiv.
change: Added DBLP as a free engineering-index layer covering ICASSP, Interspeech, ACL and ACM metadata, with a per-family DBLP query and a contract test.
reason: IEEE Xplore, ACM DL, ACL Anthology and the ISCA Archive require subscriptions or offer no usable search API; DBLP indexes their metadata and is free. The false-negative audit (FNA-009 to 012) had already shown engineering venues were being missed.
impact_on_review: Closes the engineering-index coverage gap without subscription access. DBLP carries no abstracts, so records need title-level screening plus a metadata lookup before extraction.

original_plan: PubMed scoped to [Title/Abstract]; Europe PMC and OpenAlex unscoped.
change: Europe PMC queries rewritten through a TITLE_ABS transform; OpenAlex switched from the bare search parameter to the title_and_abstract.search filter.
reason: The three sources were answering different questions, so their counts were not comparable. OpenAlex bare search returned 38,473 records for the phrase voice biomarker against 232 scoped, because it treats the query largely as a bag of words over full text.
impact_on_review: Counts are now comparable across sources and small enough to retrieve completely. This is the same class of defect as the malformed arXiv query in DEV-008: a source-specific query dialect used without verification.

original_plan: Packet drawn from seven hard-coded PubMed and Europe PMC preprint buckets in API return order, with inclusion decided by a keyword list.
change: Stratified proportional sampling across every (source, query family) bucket with a one-record floor; within-bucket order by SHA-256 of the record identity; keyword list demoted to advisory topic_hint_flags and off_scope_hint_flags; title_screen_decision left empty for a human.
reason: OpenAlex, arXiv and DBLP records could never reach screening; taking the first N of each bucket inherited API ranking as a hidden sampling decision; and because the keyword list named specific diseases it partly manufactured the observed 72 percent neurology concentration.
impact_on_review: Screening decisions now require a human against the eligibility criteria. Prior abstract-level tags in extraction-ready-includes.csv were produced under the old procedure and are reported as an upper bound on concentration in the synthesis.

original_plan: Bespoke rubric described as operationalizing a Mohamed-style reproducibility pattern.
change: Rubric mapped element by element to V3/V3+ (validation lens), PROBAST (risk of bias), and TRIPOD+AI (model reporting); risk-of-bias domains labelled with their PROBAST parent; Mohamed work demoted to a worked example of reporting style.
reason: The validation lens was V3 without citing it, and the risk-of-bias domains restate PROBAST. Presenting established instruments as a bespoke rubric is uncheckable by reviewers, and none of the Mohamed papers concerns voice.
impact_on_review: No change to what is assessed; the assessment is now checkable against published standards. Where rubric and instrument disagree, the instrument governs.

original_plan: Eight seeds; no cardiovascular, neurological, benchmark, prior-review, or non-English seed.
change: Added five seeds: Tsanas 2010 (neurological empirical), Luz 2020 ADReSS (benchmark), Sara 2022 (cardiovascular), Hecker 2022 (prior overlapping review), Mou 2025 (Mandarin-language).
reason: The seed set violated the minimum categories in reproducibility-and-governance.md section 1, leaving the false-negative audit blind in the strata where the corpus is densest.
impact_on_review: Thirteen seeds now cover every required category. Four of the five new seeds were absent from the 10,347-record Stage 2 corpus, which quantifies the coverage gap the DBLP layer is meant to close.

original_plan: Review positioned with an implicit expectation of continued updating.
change: Positioned explicitly as a reproducible snapshot with a stated search date (1 September 2026) and no update commitment. The words living, continuously updated, and rolling are prohibited in describing it.
reason: Currency and reproducibility trade against each other. A snapshot whose queries and raw exports are preserved lets any later reader re-execute the identical search and measure the delta, which is a stronger guarantee than an unverifiable claim of being current.
impact_on_review: No change to methods or findings. Changes how the work is described and removes an open-ended maintenance obligation.

original_plan: Deployed emergency-call and call-centre triage systems were not considered.
change: Added a section reporting this literature as context, with seven verified references, and stated the resulting scope tension explicitly.
reason: The most clinically validated use of speech in medicine, including the only randomised trial in the domain (NCT04219306, 169,049 calls), analyses conversation content via speech recognition rather than voice acoustics, so the eligibility criteria exclude it. The criteria therefore select against precisely the evidence the review reports as missing.
impact_on_review: The snapshot retains the narrow acoustic scope and reports the excluded literature as context rather than as included evidence. Widening the concept to speech-based clinical decision support regardless of acoustic or lexical feature is recorded as the principal candidate for a scope revision.
